summary: Remote WebSocket peer obtains PTY shell and full-host administration on installer
details: The agent connects to a configurable WebSocket server and routes server-sent messages to handlers that grant the remote party full control of the installer host. terminal.js spawns a local OS shell via node-pty (process.env.SHELL or bash on Unix, PowerShell/cmd on Windows) and connection/index.js handleTerminalInput writes remote bytes unmodified into the PTY (term.pty.write(msg.data)), yielding interactive command execution as the user running the agent. message-router.js additionally dispatches server-originated messages to handlers that write, delete, and move files, run git operations, mutate ~/.yeaft/config.json and MCP configuration, and invoke handleUpgradeAgent (which runs `npm install <pkgName>@latest` and rewrites the systemd/launchd unit) — so the remote side can also modify installer files, reconfigure MCP, and force the agent to upgrade to whatever version npm currently resolves. Auth is a user-configured shared secret; the SERVER_URL is configurable, so anyone controlling the configured server holds these primitives. Startup additionally performs an unpinned `git clone`/`git pull --ff-only` of https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/ and enables it in ~/.claude/settings.json, so whatever HEAD of that mutable branch points at becomes an auto-enabled Claude plugin on every start.
